notes: EIGHT BLOCKS, EIGHT `sections` ROWS, EIGHT BANDS — why, what, options, process, design,
cost, why-us, faq — in exactly the order of the eight template bands. No tenth and no
ninth: this page has no smile gallery (no service-specific before/after photography exists,
so the band was never built) and no <LocalTrust>, so there is no `gallery_marquee` row and
no `code_section` row. Nothing here touches vs-content-model.php or CodeSectionBlock.astro.
BAND VOCABULARY IS THE PILOT'S ON THIS PAGE, AND THE TEMPLATE'S OWN COMMENTS SAID
OTHERWISE. `.section.alt` is CHARCOAL (full-mouth-rehabilitation.css:228 ->
var(--vs-charcoal-green)) and `.section.dark` is SAGE-PALE (:237 -> var(--vs-sage-pale)).
Before this migration the band comments in the .astro read "(cream)" and "(sage)" — four
bands' worth of wrong, and both are real BLOCK_BANDS choices painting different tokens, so
reading the map's values off those comments instead of off the sheet would have repainted
`what`, `design`, `why-us` and `process`. Every `band` below is read off THIS stylesheet
and every one names the rule in `band_evidence`. The .astro comments are corrected in the
same commit as this file.
TWO BANDS THAT NO REGISTERED LAYOUT REPRODUCES, AND BOTH ARE MARKUP FAULTS RATHER THAN
MISSING FIELDS. `cost` is a `.cost-card` — a two-column card with a counter-numbered
`.cost-list` <ul> on the left and `.cost-body` prose on the right — and `why-us` is a
`.why-4up` 2x2 grid whose card label is a `<span class="tag">`. Both are page-local
micro-patterns the stylesheet's own header calls out as page-local (lines 9-14). Each is
mapped to the layout that carries every WORD of it, and each carries a `known_gaps` naming
exactly what the shell loses and what would close it. Read the `cost` one first: it is the
larger of the two and the one a reviewer should decide about before the backfill runs.
`cost` IS NOT A pricing_tiers BAND, AND THE CHECK WAS MADE RATHER THAN ASSUMED. That layout
draws its own <section> around a <PricingTiers> plan grid — the shape porcelain-veneers and
the four implant pages ship as a standalone `<section id="cost">`. This band has no plan, no
price, no tier and no financing line: it has three cost FACTORS and two closing sentences.
Mapping it to `pricing_tiers` would draw an empty `.plan-grid` and drop every word of the
card. See the `cost` block's `why_not_pricing_tiers` and `known_gaps`.
THE `why-us` CARDS ARE CMS ROWS AND ARE MOVED, NOT TRANSCRIBED. The live `cards` repeater
holds exactly four rows, all in group `whyUsCards`, and their meta/title/body match the
hardcoded `whyUsCards` array in the template's frontmatter character-for-character —
verified live, all four. They are the only `cards` rows this page has, which is why every
other card, tier and point below is a literal transcribed from the template.
THE TWO OTHER REPEATERS ARE MOVED IN FULL: 3 `process_steps` rows (Step One through Step
Three) by `process`, and 2 `faqs` rows by `faq`. Both counts verified live. The faq answers
carry inline <a class="vs-link"> markup and both the template (:588) and FaqBlock render
the answer with set:html, so the switch is invisible.
TWO EYEBROWS THAT LOOK LIKE LITERALS AND ARE NOT. The template hardcodes `Treatment
Options` (:368) and `Treatment Planning` (:448), and the live CMS `options` and `design`
rows hold those same two strings. So they are `{ "section": "eyebrow" }` — moved, not
re-typed. The one eyebrow that IS a literal is `process`: that row's eyebrow comes back
null, so without the literal the eyebrow disappears on migration.
CTA ROWS SPLIT THE SAME TWO WAYS AS ALL THREE MIGRATED SIBLINGS, and the split is the
components' decision, not this file's. `options` and `process` draw their rows entirely
from the component and their layouts have no cta sub-fields, so nothing is supplied for
them; `what` and `faq` gate their row on cta_label being filled, so those two carry a
transcribed pair. All eight `sections` rows on this page return ctaLabel and ctaHref null —
verified live — so there was never anything to move.
THE RAIL IS THE SAME LIST ON BOTH SIDES OF THE SWITCH. The eight live `toc_links` rows run
why, what, options, process, design, cost, why-us, faq — the template's order exactly — and
every one of the eight anchors is claimed by a block below. `why-us` passes the derived
rail's selector test (a hyphen is legal everywhere but the first character), so the derived
rail is all eight entries in the same order the repeater lists them.

<section class="section"> around a .section-head and an imported <PricingTiers> plan
grid (PricingTiersBlock.astro:239-253), which is what porcelain-veneers and the four
implant pages ship as a standalone <section id="cost">.
This band is a <section class="section" id="cost"> around a .section-head and a
a .cost-list <ul> and a .cost-body pair of paragraphs. The OUTER shell matches; the
inner one is a different component entirely.
And there is nothing to put in the layout. `plans` wants name, price, meta,
price_note, price_suffix, ribbon, highlighted and a `features` list of lines; this
band names no plan and quotes no figure — its three rows are cost FACTORS (what
changes the number) and its two paragraphs are a closing promise. `note`, the
financing line, is the one field that has a plausible tenant, and the sentence it
would take is already one of the three <li>. A `pricing_tiers` row here would draw an
empty plan grid and drop the card whole.
So the band is mapped to `stat_callout`, whose shell IS this shape's near relative —

StatCalloutBlock's <ul> draws a sage rule instead of a counter, which is part of the shell gap below.

known_gaps: OPEN, AND THIS IS THE BAND A REVIEWER SHOULD DECIDE ABOUT BEFORE THE BACKFILL RUNS.
EVERY WORD SURVIVES. The section-head is the CMS `cost` row (eyebrow "Investment",
heading and body all non-null — verified live); the three cost factors are the `points`
rows above, lead and body each; the two closing sentences are `intro` and `intro_2`.
Nothing leaves the page. What changes is the shell, in five specific ways:
1. THE CARD IS ONE COLUMN INSTEAD OF TWO. .fmrehab .cost-card is
`grid-template-columns: 1.05fr 1fr` with a 60px gap and a border-right rule down
the middle (full-mouth-rehabilitation.css:490-503). StatCalloutBlock's
.lasting-card is `auto 1fr` and, with no stat to fill the first track, the
.lasting-body is the only child in the grid. The vertical divider goes with it.
2. THE LIST MOVES BELOW THE PROSE. The template reads list-then-prose across two
columns; StatCalloutBlock's card is <h3>, intro, intro_2, <ul> in that fixed
order, so the three factors come after the two closing sentences. That inverts
the band's argument: it currently reads "here is what drives the number, and here
is our promise about it".
3. THREE CLASS NAMES CHANGE. .cost-card -> .lasting-card, .cost-list -> (gone, the
<ul> sits directly in .lasting-body), .cost-body -> .lasting-body. The page sheet
styles none of the .lasting-* names — they were renamed when this page was built
(stylesheet header, lines 9-11) — so the band would be painted entirely by
StatCalloutBlock's own scoped rules, which is a different white card, not an
unstyled one.
4. THE 01/02/03 MARKERS BECOME BULLET RULES. The counter-generated leading-zero
numbers (full-mouth-rehabilitation.css:507-514) have no counterpart in the
block's <ul>, which draws a small sage rule per item.
5. THREE COLONS APPEAR. See `no_trailing_colon` above.
WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT IS MARKUP, NOT A FIELD, AND THE COMPONENT ALREADY SAYS SO.
StatCalloutBlock.astro:11 names `.cost-card` and `.insurance-card` as near variants of
the `.lasting-card` shell that join in a later phase without a redesign. Closing this
means a shell variant on stat_callout — one select whose choices are the three card
names, driving the wrapper classes and whether the list takes the first track or
follows the prose — plus the `.cost-card` rules moved into the block's scoped sheet.
That is a component change plus a PHP select, in one commit, and then this block gains
one field. It is NOT a case for a tenth layout: one shell with three skins is the
trade the layout was built for.
DO NOT CLOSE IT BY REACHING FOR pricing_tiers. See `why_not_pricing_tiers` above —
that layout draws a plan grid this band has no plans for, and would drop the card
whole rather than restyle it.
THE RAIL ENTRY SURVIVES EITHER WAY: the live toc_links carry anchor `cost` labelled
"Cost", claimed by this block's section_id, so it keeps its place between "Smile
Design" and "Why Vivid Smiles" — and unlike teeth-whitening, the label does not
promise prices the band does not show. This band has never quoted a figure.

known_gaps: OPEN, AND SMALLER THAN THE `cost` ONE: THE WORDS ALL SURVIVE, THE SHELL DOES NOT.
Eyebrow, heading and body are the CMS `why-us` row; all four cards are the CMS
